A couple extra practical notes:

- **Order matters**: EQ before compression cleans up problem frequencies before they get squashed and locked in; compression before reverb keeps the reverb tail from getting pumped unpredictably.
- **Reference against real footage**: A/B against actual beach-walking footage or field recordings if you have any — it's the fastest way to catch when the high-shelf "sizzle" is overdone (sounds artificial/hissy) versus just enough.
- **Don't overdo the splash layer volume**: it should read as a texture under the footstep, not compete with it — if you can hear the splash before the foot's transient, pull it back 2-3dB.
